A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same d-RRMDP/R2PVI research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figures 2–3 report original simulations measuring policy robustness, regularization sensitivity and computational time.

after.justification: Section 6 and Figures 1–2 retain original simulation results for the linear MDP and American put option environments.

M1.justification: v2 Algorithm 1 adds a general f-divergence estimation procedure using regression of the conjugate function f* followed by optimization over α; v1 assumed an estimation oracle. The existing TV, KL and χ² estimators are retained in v2 Algorithm 2 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same simulated linear MDP and American put option tasks under the same environmental perturbations. The option robustness panel moves from v1 Figure 3(b) to v2 Figure 1(d); it is not a new scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain PEVI, DRPVI and DRVI-L, with the same participation in the corresponding robustness and timing comparisons. Both versions explicitly exclude P2MPO and DROP from experiments.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A retain the linear-MDP sample size of 100, horizons of 3 and 20, feature constructions, experimental hyperparameters, and timing sweeps over sample size and feature dimension. No experimental protocol revision is reported.

E4.justification: The same environmental perturbation tests, λ/ρ sensitivity comparisons and computational scaling analyses remain. Regrouping the figures does not introduce additional ablations or robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions retain shaded reward bands and Appendix A.2's timing averages over five repetitions. No seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance testing is added or revised.

E6.justification: v1 Figure 2(c) assigns the rising blue reward curve to R2PVI and the falling orange curve to DRPVI. v2 Figure 1(c) reverses these method assignments, changing the reported method-specific trends. The remaining empirical results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1.3 restores a missing 1/(4λ) factor in the χ² second-moment error term and propagates the correction through Theorem 5.1, Corollary 5.4 and Table 1. The table's χ² bound changes its H/λ factor from H³(1+1/λ) to H²(1+H/λ). Section 4 also adds the general conjugate-duality formula; most other proofs and assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central framework and theoretical contributions remain. However, v2's contribution summary drops v1's explicit TV/KL restriction on efficiency comparable to standard linear-MDP algorithms, while its abstract broadens the efficiency comparison from constrained-DRMDP methods to baseline methods generally.

C2.justification: New Remark 4.2 explains numerical difficulties with general conjugate optimization and the need for divergence-specific designs. Section 6 also moderates v1's claim that experiments verify exact DRMDP/RRMDP value-function equivalence, emphasizing analogous parameter roles and matched performance instead.

D1.justification: v2 Section 6 adds an implementation repository link. Hardware specifications, feature construction and experimental hyperparameters were already documented in v1 and are retained.

R1.justification: Several references are added, including Satia and Lave (1973), Guo et al. (2024), Liu and Xu (2025), and Xiong et al. (2022). The χ² motivation replaces Lee et al. (2021) with Panaganti and Kalathil (2022) and Xu et al. (2023). The central positioning against unstructured regularization remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the main exposition are rewritten, and the algorithm narrative is reorganized around general and specialized procedures. Hard-instance motivation moves to Appendix D, references move before the appendices, and conference front matter, acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main text and extensively reflows equations, tables and algorithm boxes. The hard-instance diagram moves to Appendix D as Figure 3. The option robustness panel joins the linear-MDP panels in Figure 1, leaving timing panels in Figure 2; legends, axes and captions also change.

improvement.justification: The corrected χ² derivation and bound, explicit general estimator, numerical-stability qualification and implementation link provide limited technical and reproducibility gains. Experimental validation remains essentially unchanged. New cross-reference errors, including calling assumptions 'Theorem', and the misleading linear-MDP caption covering an option-task panel temper the presentation benefits.
